title: Protocol to visualize a bodily map of musical uncertainty and prediction
author: Daikoku, Tanaka

steps.title: Down‑sample coordinate data
steps.instruction: Reduce the raw x‑ and y‑coordinate data by a factor of 40; the original body‑image template is 871 px wide by 1920 px high.

steps.title: Generate bodily map
steps.instruction: Create a colour‑coded bodily map from the down‑sampled coordinates using MATLAB 2022b’s contourf function.

steps.title: Extract click counts per region
steps.instruction: For each participant, count the total number of clicks that fall within the predefined cardiac and abdominal regions.

substeps.instruction: Define the cardiac region as pixels 360–550 (width) by 390–620 (height).
Define the abdominal region as pixels 360–510 (width) by 650–850 (height).

steps.title: Run GLMM analysis
steps.instruction: Fit a generalized linear mixed model with the formula Abdomen ~ Heart + (1|Subjects), where ‘Abdomen’ is the response, ‘Heart’ the predictor, and ‘Subjects’ a random intercept for each participant.

steps.title: Test normality of click data
steps.instruction: Perform the Shapiro–Wilk test on the total click counts for the cardiac, abdominal, and head positions for each participant.

steps.title: Compare click and emotion scores
steps.instruction: According to the Shapiro–Wilk results, apply either a parametric repeated‑measures ANOVA or a non‑parametric Friedman repeated‑measures ANOVA to compare click counts (cardiac, abdominal, head) and the scores for valence, arousal, and categorical emotional responses across the eight chord‑progression types.

steps.title: Score emotional categories
steps.instruction: Assign points to the five highest‑ranked emotional categories (5 points for first, 4 for second, 3 for third, 2 for fourth, 1 for fifth) and compute the average score for each of the 33 emotion categories across all participants.

steps.title: Test normality of emotion scores
steps.instruction: Conduct the Shapiro–Wilk test on the 33 categorical emotion scores and on the valence and arousal scores obtained from the nine‑point dimensional judgments.

steps.title: Analyze emotion and click data
steps.instruction: Based on the normality test, run either a parametric repeated‑measures ANOVA or a non‑parametric Friedman repeated‑measures ANOVA to compare total clicks (cardiac, abdominal, head) and the valence, arousal, and categorical emotion scores across the eight chord‑progression types.
